quote.text: The difference here between the Epicurean and our own school is this: our wise man feels his troubles but overcomes them, while their wise man does not even feel them. We share with them the belief that the wise man is content with himself. Nevertheless, self-sufficient though he is, he still desires a friend, a neighbour, a companion. Notice how self-contented he is: on occasion such a man is content with a mere partial self – if he loses a hand as a result of war or disease, or has one of his eyes, or even both, put out in an accident, he will be satisfied with what remains of himself and be no less pleased with his body now that it is maimed and incomplete than he was when it was whole. But while he does not hanker after what he has lost, he does prefer not to lose them. And this is what we mean when we say the wise man is self-content; he is so in the sense that he is able to do without friends, not that he desires to do without them. When I speak of his being ‘able’ to do this, what I am saying in fact amounts to this: he bears the loss of a friend with equanimity.
quote.author: Seneca
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood:
    • Embrace imperfections as a natural part of life; in parenting, acknowledge that both you and your children face challenges, yet each setback is an opportunity to cultivate inner strength and resilience.
    • Lead by example in managing adversity with grace; just as the wise man accepts his losses without despair, use every familial trial as a lesson in growing compassion and self-contentment.
  • Leadership:
    • Practice stoic resilience by confronting obstacles head-on; a true leader recognizes that even amid loss or failure, it is our response that ultimately shapes our character and inspires others.
    • Nurture authentic connections within your team; while a leader may be self-sufficient, the mutual support of trusted peers and colleagues fosters an environment where collective wisdom can flourish.
  • Product Management:
    • View product setbacks as opportunities for growth; like the wise man who accepts bodily imperfections without losing his purpose, a product manager should adapt to challenges, refining offerings with a calm and focused mind.
    • Build a collaborative spirit within your team; encourage open dialogue and supportive relationships that help everyone bear the strain of failure with equanimity, leading to continuous innovation and improvement.
